title: Every introenumerable set contains a uniformly introreducible subset
summary: We prove that every infinite introenumerable set contains an infinite uniformly introreducible subset, answering both parts of Question 1.7 of Greenberg, Harrison-Trainor, Patey, and Turetsky affirmatively. Moreover, a single procedure computes the original set from every infinite subset of the selected set. The proof combines the uniformization and refinement results of these authors with Ramsey-theoretic methods and a canonical reconstruction argument. We also obtain refinements controlling the ordinals and hyperjumps of the selected subsets.
